To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UVA, UVC, and UVB irradiated, mitogenic‐activated human peripheral blood mononuclear leukocytes exhibit a dose dependent reduction in their proliferative response.
the effects of UVB and UVA on lymphoblast transformation and [3H]thymidine uptake are distinct.
the three major wavebands of UV radiation interfere with the proliferative response of human lymphocytes to mitogens, and that each waveband has its own characteristic pattern of inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of UV on human lymphocytes in vitro.
the effects of UV on human peripheral blood lymphocytes in vitro, specifically on the response of these cells to mitogen.
the effects of ultraviolet radiation on human peripheral blood mononuclear cell function and the role of ultraviolet radiation in the etiology of cutaneous T cell lymphoma (CTCL).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UVB and UVA are more damaging than UVC to mitogen stimulated human lymphocytes.
UVA is more damaging to human peripheral lymphocytes than UVB or UVA.
UVA is the most effective waveband in inhibiting the response of human peripheral blood mononuclear cell to mitogens, with UVB and UCA being less effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of UV on human lymphocytes are complex and dependent upon the dose and wavelength of UV, the time in culture and the cell population studied.
the UV wavebands tested here have a differential effect on the various stages of mitogen‐induced blast transformation and that UVA is the most effective in inhibiting blastogenesis and DNA synthesis.

UVA, which is the most abundant of the UV wavelengths in sunlight, interfered with blast transformation and DNA synthesis in mitogen‐ stimulated cultures to a greater degree than did UVB or UCV, which are less abundant in sunlight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UV radiation can inhibit the proliferative response of lymphocytes to mitogens.
the effects of ultraviolet radiation on the immune system are not all the same.
the effect of UV radiation on lymphocytes in culture may not be a good model for the effect of UV on the immune system in vivo, where the effects of UV are more complex.
